hero.heading: Everything a homelab needs, in one platform you own.
hero.lead: Compute, storage and networking, with upgrades and clustering built in. One console, one CLI and one API on every node.

tide.heading: Full VMs when you need them. A microVM for every app.
tide.lead: Start from an ISO or disk image and you get a full VM. Start from a container image or a Compose file and you get an app, isolated in its own microVM with its own kernel.

items.title: Full VMs
items.body: QEMU with KVM: UEFI, virtual TPM, Secure Boot and a VNC console in the browser. Windows 11 installs out of the box.

items.title: Apps in microVMs
items.body: Kata Containers on Cloud Hypervisor by default, or isolation: shared for a plain container.

items.title: App catalog
items.body: One-click apps from curated, community templates. Import any Compose file.

items.title: Passthrough
items.body: USB, disk and GPU passthrough, including a shared iGPU for media transcoding.

items.title: Templates and cloud-init
items.body: Build a VM once, clone it many times, configure it on first boot.

items.title: Updates and secrets
items.body: See new image versions, update with rollback, and inject secrets safely.

reef.heading: ZFS and Btrfs, shares and backups that restore.
reef.lead: Both file systems are first-class. Pools feed VM disks, app volumes, shares and object storage, and backups run on a schedule you set once.

items.title: Pools
items.body: ZFS and Btrfs pools with snapshots, scrubs and SMART disk health.

items.title: Shares and S3
items.body: SMB and NFS shares, plus S3-compatible buckets with Garage.

items.title: Backups
items.body: Scheduled, incremental, deduplicated backups of VMs and apps with rustic.

items.title: Databases
items.body: Managed PostgreSQL for your apps, with point-in-time restore.

items.title: Encryption at rest
items.body: ZFS native encryption or LUKS under Btrfs, unlocked by the TPM.

items.title: Platform backup
items.body: Export and restore Crustates' own state, so a dead boot disk isn't fatal.

current.heading: Every app on HTTPS, every packet accounted for.
current.lead: Bridges and VLANs, a firewall per app, flow logs, and local names with certificates. No port forwarding needed for remote access.

items.title: Networks
items.body: Bridges, VLANs and bonds, with DHCP and IP management for IPv4 and IPv6.

items.title: eBPF policy
items.body: Per-workload firewall rules, flow logs and metrics, built on Aya.

items.title: Ingress and TLS
items.body: Caddy as the reverse proxy: a local CA by default, or Let's Encrypt for your own domain.

items.title: Local names
items.body: Every app gets <name>.crust.internal, plus mDNS on your LAN.

items.title: Remote access
items.body: NetBird first, Tailscale or Headscale as an option.

items.title: Host firewall
items.body: nftables protects the host itself, before anything else starts.

molt.heading: Upgrade the whole system as one image.
molt.body: A read-only, image-based OS. Updates arrive as one signed image with stable and beta channels, and you can roll back in one step from the console or the local recovery screen.
points: Offline updates from a USB stick

cast.heading: Join a second machine without port forwarding.
cast.body: Start with one node. Add another at home, at a relative's place or on a VPS, and manage them as one. Nodes find each other by key, not by IP address.
points: crust cast join with a one-time token

barnacle.heading: Extend it safely.
barnacle.lead: Barnacle plugins are sandboxed Wasm components. Each one gets only the permissions you approve, so a broken plugin can't take down your host.

items.title: Event hooks
items.body: On VM created, register it in DNS.

items.title: Custom drivers
items.body: Storage, backup or network backends.

items.title: Policy checks
items.body: Rules that run before any change.

items.title: Dashboard widgets
items.body: Your own panels in the console.

spawn.heading: Your homelab, in a Git repo.
spawn.lead: Keep apps, VMs and network as YAML in GitHub, Forgejo or GitLab. Every pull request gets a plan; merging applies it. Push your own code and Crustates builds and deploys it.

items.title: Pull-based sync
items.body: Polls your repo and reacts to webhooks. No port forwarding.

items.title: Plan on every PR
items.body: A dry run posted as a comment. Merge to apply.

items.title: Drift and secrets
items.body: Drift detection, plus SOPS + age secrets decrypted only on the node.

items.title: Push-to-deploy
items.body: Builds with BuildKit or Railpack, with preview apps for pull requests.

assistant.heading: Ask your homelab what's going on. Then let it fix it.
assistant.lead: A built-in assistant that reads live state, metrics and logs through the same API you use. It runs on a local model by default, acts with your role, and shows every change as a plan you confirm.

mock.question: Why is Jellyfin buffering tonight?
mock.where: llama.cpp on node-1 · stayed on your network
mock.answer: The jellyfin microVM has hit its 2 vCPU limit since 20:14 while transcoding 4K. The iGPU isn't passed through, so transcoding runs on the CPU.
mock.offer: I can pass through the iGPU and restart the app. That's a 30-second outage.

api.heading: One declarative API behind everything.
api.lead: Every resource has a spec and a status. The console, crust CLI, terminal UI, OpenTofu provider and MCP server are all clients of the same API, documented with Scalar at /docs on every node.

engines.heading: Proven open source, with Rust where it matters.
engines.lead: Crustates' own code is the control plane, the node agent and the drivers. Each engine sits behind a trait, so it can be swapped later.
